abstract: Reconstructing individual microglia from confocal images is challenging when fine processes have weak fluorescence or neighboring cells form connected structures. Inspired by Grady's random-walker framework, we propose a soma-guided probabilistic method for three-dimensional microglial reconstruction and cell-of-origin assignment. Signal-weighted random walks quantify voxel connectivity to each soma by the probability of reaching that soma before background or another soma. A path-length adjustment reduces the penalty on distal processes. Adjusted scores are compared across somata to assign voxels, subject to score and image-intensity thresholds. We assess process recovery and cell assignment separately using exact three-dimensional matching to manual tracings. In a P28 single-cell example, the reconstruction covered 83.98% of traced voxels within the analyzed region. For a connected cell pair in sample 12hrMD82, coverage was 71.86% and 82.31%, with a pooled incorrect-assignment rate of 4.61% among detected traced voxels. Local analyses were also combined to produce an overview of 13 cell reconstructions in the same sample. We additionally provide a two-dimensional version that tolerates short signal gaps in maximum-intensity projections. These initial examples demonstrate the potential of soma-specific connectivity for microglial reconstruction.
